adapters.exportDuty: Leaves with us: every row of every table. The nightly export (services/platform/src/backup/) writes each D1 database to R2 as gzipped JSON lines — its schema, every row in rowid order, its indexes — and the schema is the plain-SQL migrations in services/platform/migrations and services/subscriptiontracker-api/migrations, so a target REPLAYS the migrations and LOADS the export; `node tooling/ops/port-switch.mjs sql --to sqlite --dry-run --env sandbox --export <file>` rehearses exactly that, read-only. Cannot move: D1-specific limits only, which a new host must match or exceed — tooling/ceilings.json d1.queriesPerInvocation, d1.maxBoundParametersPerQuery, d1.maxDatabaseSize, d1.storagePerAccount, d1.databasesPerAccount and d1.rowsWrittenPerDay — and D1's authorizer, whose refusals tooling/ops/check-d1-accepts-live-sql.mjs measures.

c8Seam.why: tooling/capability-register.json records Cloudflare's C-8 seam as the client's ConfigTransport — the client's seam onto the Worker host, the substrate README section 7 keeps. D1 was the last Cloudflare surface the kv, objects and ratelimit registries waited on (their c8Seam until: port-sql); with four Cloudflare ports and one C-8 seam per vendor, re-seating it is a cross-register decision this train records and does not take.

adapters.exportDuty: An engine, not a store of record: node:sqlite in memory for one test, or one local file for the export dry run. Nothing of ours lives in it, so nothing to export; it is the TARGET the dry run loads an export into.

pending.case: prepare-bind-first — first() of a bound read, and null for no row. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario

all-returns-rows — all() answers every matching row in the order asked, [] for none. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario
run-reports-changes — run() meta.changes counts the rows a write touched. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario

bind-returns-a-new-statement — one statement bound twice in one batch writes two rows. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario

batch-answers-in-order — one result per batched statement, a read answering its rows. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario

undefined-bind-is-refused — an undefined bind is refused as D1_TYPE_ERROR and writes nothing. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario

unique-violation-is-classified — D1's own UNIQUE failure reads as isUniqueViolation and never as transient. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario

transient-error-is-retried — a reset worded as workerd words it is retried once by withD1Retry. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario

deterministic-error-is-not-retried — D1's own deterministic failure is sent once. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario
batch-is-atomic — one failing statement rolls the whole batch back. Not run against D1: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the live check, which runs no scenario

_why: PLATFORM_DB, SUBSCRIPTIONTRACKER_DB and APP_DB are declared as SqlDb in every Worker's `interface Env` (and the brick's), and every handler, route, lib and middleware — the shared helpers in services/_shared/src/d1.ts, erasure.ts and entitlement-read.ts included — takes a SqlDb or a SqlStatement. The binding satisfies the port STRUCTURALLY; cloudflareD1 is the identity, kept as the compile-time proof (tsc reds the day the binding and the port drift). assert-ports limb 12 refuses a D1Database, D1PreparedStatement or D1Result type anywhere else under services/*/src.
The surface is what the code calls, derived from every `.prepare(` site: prepare, bind, first(), all, run, batch. No raw, exec, dump or withSession — nothing calls them.

L2 claimed, L3 target. The selection is by environment (wrangler binds D1 in live and sandbox; the sqlite engine serves tests), no caller imports an adapter, and one non-fake adapter is live. The conformance suite runs against the sqlite engine — the node:sqlite engine every Worker suite already ran its SQL through, promoted from services/platform/test/harness.ts — in every Worker's npm test. Against D1 every scenario is PENDING: no Worker suite runs on workerd, and D1's conformance file is the credentialled live check (kind `live`), which proves D1 ACCEPTS the statements this repository sends and runs none of the scenarios. L3 needs a second adapter with zero pending: a workerd-backed run (Miniflare or the vitest pool) of the same suite would earn it.
Export duty: the nightly R2 export plus the migrations. A Postgres exit is a dialect question (the switch runbook), not a code change behind this port.
